mainTopic: Children of a נדה, סוטה and שומרת יבם, and מנשה's trial of ישעיה
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing אביי's statement that everyone agrees a child from a נדה or a סוטה is not a ממזר, because קידושין take effect with both women. A ברייתא supports him and adds a third case, a שומרת יבם. The גמרא explains that אביי left her out because he was unsure whether the הלכה follows רב or שמואל about קידושין with her. Next the גמרא turns to שמעון בן עזאי's lineage scroll from the משנה, which also said that מנשה killed ישעיה. רבא tells how מנשה put ישעיה on trial, charging that three of his prophecies contradict the תורה of משה. ישעיה chose not to answer, escaped into a cedar, and died when the saw reached his mouth. The גמרא then answers the contradictions. ישעיה saw through an unclear glass while only משה saw clearly. A community is always answered, while an individual is answered especially in the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכיפורים. The third contradiction depends on a disagreement between תנאים, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of אביי's statement: a סוטה's child is not a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The last words of אביי's ruling: everyone agrees that a child born from relations with a סוטה, like a נדה, is not a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and with a סוטה, that the child is not a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of אביי's statement. Everyone agrees that relations with a נדה or a סוטה do not produce a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the תנאים argued about which forbidden relationships produce a ממזר. אביי points out two cases where every side agrees there is no ממזר, even though the relationship is forbidden. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: A married woman suspected of being unfaithful, who is forbidden to her husband
A child born from certain forbidden relationships, who may not marry into the general community

phrases.english: or with a sota,
that the child is not a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's statement, which began just before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All opinions agree that a child from a נדה or a סוטה is not a ממזר.

steps.title: Why a נדה's child is not a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: קידושין take effect with a נדה, as the פסוק 'ותהי נדתה עליו' shows. So her child is not a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נדה: קידושין take effect with her, as it says, 'And her impurity shall be upon him.' Even while she is a נדה, קידושין with her take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of אביי's statement. A נדה's child is not a ממזר because קידושין with her are valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule assumed here is that a ממזר comes only from a woman with whom קידושין cannot take effect. The word 'ותהי' (shall be) is read as a hint to marriage. So even during her נדה time, a man can marry her. That puts her outside the ממזר category.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual period, forbidden for relations
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
And it shall be, read here as hinting at marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Relations with a נדה are a serious איסור כרת. The child is still not a ממזר, because what matters here is whether קידושין can take effect, not how severe the איסור is.

phrases.english: A menstruating woman, since betrothal takes effect with her,
as it is said: "And her impurity shall be upon him,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24. The words 'shall be' are what hint at marriage taking effect.

phrases.english: even at the time of her impurity
betrothal takes effect with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and the source for the נדה part of אביי's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין take effect with a נדה, so her child is not a ממזר.

steps.title: Why a סוטה's child is not a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The same reason works for a סוטה: קידושין take effect with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A סוטה too: קידושין take effect with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of אביי's statement. A סוטה is like a נדה, because קידושין with her are valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוטה is forbidden to her husband, but this איסור is not the kind that stops קידושין from taking effect. So the same rule applies: where קידושין take effect, the child is not a ממזר.

phrases.english: A sota too,
since betrothal takes effect with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹטָה נָמֵי דְּהָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִידּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning from the נדה case to the סוטה case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין take effect with a סוטה, so her child is not a ממזר.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי and adds the שומרת יבם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same as אביי: everyone agrees that a child from a נדה, a סוטה, or a שומרת יבם is not a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: Everyone agrees that one who has relations with a נדה, a סוטה, or a שומרת יבם, the child is not a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as אביי. This backs up his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא matches אביי's two cases and adds a third, a שומרת יבם (a widow waiting for יבום). The words 'הכל מודים' show that even the תנאים who argue about ממזר agree on these cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום

steps.whatToRemember: A ממזר comes only from a relationship where קידושין cannot take effect. A נדה, a סוטה, and a שומרת יבם are all forbidden, yet their children are not ממזרים, and all opinions agree on this.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that being a forbidden relationship is not enough to make a child a ממזר. The test is whether קידושין could take effect.

phrases.english: This is also taught:
All agree regarding one who has relations with a menstruating woman
or with a sota, or with a widow waiting for her yavam,
that the child is not a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that confirms אביי's statement from steps 1 to 3.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that a child from a נדה or a סוטה is not a ממזר according to all opinions
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that everyone agrees a child from a נדה, a סוטה, or a שומרת יבם is not a ממזר

steps.title: Why אביי did not mention a woman waiting for יבום
steps.stepSummary: אביי left out שומרת יבם because he was unsure whether קידושין by another man take effect with her. That question is a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי did not mention a שומרת יבם because he was unsure whether the הלכה follows רב or שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא listed three women: נדה, סוטה and שומרת יבם. אביי listed only the first two, and the גמרא explains why he left out the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reason was that קידושין take effect with these women, so the child is not a ממזר. For a שומרת יבם it is unclear whether another man's קידושין take effect: רב says no, and שמואל says maybe. Since אביי was unsure, he could not include her with confidence.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה
Whether it follows רב or שמואל

steps.whatToRemember: אביי agrees with the ברייתא about נדה and סוטה. He only held back on שומרת יבם because he was unsure whether קידושין take effect with her.

phrases.english: And Abaye: a woman waiting for her yavam,
he is unsure about her,
whether it follows Rav or Shmuel.
phrases.notes: רב says קידושין from another man don't take effect with her; שמואל says they might.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question raised by the ברייתא in step 4: why did אביי leave out the שומרת יבם?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the missing case as a matter of doubt, not disagreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think אביי disagrees with the ברייתא about שומרת יבם
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי simply did not know whether קידושין take effect with her, because of the מחלוקת between רב and שמואל

steps.title: בן עזאי's lineage scroll and what was written in it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words of שמעון בן עזאי, then brings a ברייתא with the fuller contents of the scroll he found in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'שמעון בן עזאי said...'. A ברייתא teaches: שמעון בן עזאי said, I found a family-lineage scroll in ירושלים. Written in it was: so-and-so is a ממזר from a married woman. Also written: the teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is small in amount but clean. Also written: מנשה killed ישעיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that tells us more of what the scroll said. The last line, about מנשה and ישעיה, sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentioned only the line about the ממזר, which supports the view that a child from אשת איש is a ממזר. The ברייתא adds two more lines: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and מנשה killed ישעיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Small in amount but clean and accurate

steps.whyThisMatters: 'משנת רבי אליעזר בן יעקב קב ונקי' is a famous rule: the הלכה generally follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said, etc.
It was taught: Shimon ben Azzai says:
I found a scroll of family lineages in Jerusalem,
and it was written in it:
So-and-so is a mamzer from a married woman,
and it was written in it:

phrases.aramaic: מִשְׁנַת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב קַב וְנָקִי.
phrases.english: The teaching of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov is a kav, but clean.
phrases.notes: A קב is a small measure, so his teachings are few, but accurate.

phrases.english: And it was written in it:
Manasseh killed Isaiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי כּוּ׳. תָּנֵי, שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The scroll recorded a ממזר from אשת איש, praised רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's teaching, and said that מנשה killed ישעיה

steps.title: רבא: מנשה put ישעיה on trial before killing him
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that מנשה did not just murder ישעיה. He first judged him in court and then killed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: he judged him, and then he killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts to explain the line 'מנשה killed ישעיה.' This sets up the next step, where we hear the charges מנשה brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's point is that the killing took the form of a trial. מנשה treated ישעיה as someone who spoke against the תורה, and only then executed him.

phrases.english: Rava said:
He judged him in court, and then killed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the scroll's line that מנשה killed ישעיה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנשה killed ישעיה after a trial, not without one

steps.title: מנשה's three charges against ישעיה
steps.stepSummary: מנשה points to three places where ישעיה's words seem to contradict משה רבינו: seeing ה׳, when ה׳ is near, and adding years to a person's life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: משה your teacher said, 'No person can see Me and live,' and you said, 'I saw ה׳ sitting on a high and lofty throne.' משה your teacher said, 'ה׳ our God is near whenever we call Him,' and you said, 'Seek ה׳ while He can be found.' משה your teacher said, 'I will fill the number of your days,' and you said, 'I will add fifteen years to your days'!
steps.whatsHappening: These are the charges at ישעיה's trial. Each time, מנשה sets a פסוק from the תורה against a statement of ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First: משה said no one can see ה׳, but ישעיה said he saw Him. Second: משה said ה׳ is near whenever we call, but ישעיה implied He can only be found at certain times. Third: משה said a person's years are fixed, but ישעיה told חזקיהו that fifteen years would be added.

phrases.english: He said to him: Moses your teacher said:
'For no person can see Me and live,'
and you said:

phrases.aramaic: ״וָאֶרְאֶה אֶת ה׳ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רָם וְנִשָּׂא״.
phrases.english: 'I saw the Lord sitting on a high and lofty throne.'
Moses your teacher said:
'Who is like the Lord our God whenever we call to Him,'
and you said:
'Seek the Lord while He can be found.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 55:6. That sounds like ה׳ is only near at certain times.

phrases.english: Moses your teacher said:
'I will fill the number of your days,'
and you said:
'I will add fifteen years to your days'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the charges at the trial that רבא mentioned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three of ישעיה's statements seem to contradict פסוקים in the תורה of משה, so מנשה treats him as a false prophet

steps.title: ישעיה chooses not to answer and escapes into a cedar
steps.stepSummary: ישעיה decides not to explain himself, because מנשה would not accept it and would then be killing him knowingly. He says a holy Name and is swallowed inside a cedar tree, which they saw apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישעיה said: I know that he won't accept what I tell him, and if I do tell him, I will turn him into a deliberate sinner. He said a Name and was swallowed into a cedar. They brought the cedar and sawed it.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering the charges, ישעיה explains to himself why he will stay silent, and then he escapes miraculously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיה could have answered, but מנשה would kill him anyway. Hearing the answer first would only make מנשה's sin more deliberate. So ישעיה kept quiet to spare him that, and tried to escape instead.
steps.confusionAlert: ישעיה's silence does not mean he had no answer. The text says he stayed quiet because מנשה would not accept any answer.

phrases.english: Isaiah said:
I know about him
that he will not accept what I tell him,
and if I do tell him,
I will make him a deliberate sinner.
phrases.notes: He would kill ישעיה anyway, but now knowing he was wrong.

phrases.english: He said a Name
and was swallowed up inside a cedar tree.
They brought the cedar and sawed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר יְשַׁעְיָה: יָדַעְנָא בֵּיהּ דְּלָא מְקַבֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ישעיה's response to the charges: a reasoned refusal to answer, then an escape
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישעיה stayed silent so that מנשה would not become a deliberate sinner, and he fled into a cedar

steps.title: ישעיה dies when the saw reaches his mouth
steps.stepSummary: ישעיה died just as the saw reached his mouth. This was a punishment for calling the Jewish people a nation of impure lips.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it reached his mouth, he died, because he had said, 'And I dwell among a people of impure lips.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with ישעיה's death, and the גמרא explains why he died at exactly that point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that his death came at the mouth is measure for measure. With his mouth he had spoken badly about the Jewish people, so his mouth was where his punishment came.
steps.whatToRemember: Even a great נביא like ישעיה was punished for speaking negatively about the Jewish people.

phrases.english: When it reached opposite his mouth,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the saw cutting through the cedar.

phrases.english: he died.
Because he had said:
'And I dwell among a people of impure lips.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מְטָא לַהֲדֵי פּוּמָּא, נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story of the sawing and explains the timing of ישעיה's death
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ישעיה's death at the mouth was a measure-for-measure punishment for speaking badly about the Jewish people

steps.title: Still, the verses contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that even though ישעיה chose not to answer מנשה, the contradictions he raised are still real and need answers.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the verses do contradict each other. How do we resolve them?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and now the גמרא turns to the actual questions. It is setting up the next steps, which will answer each of מנשה's three contradictions one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ישעיה chose not to defend himself, so the story leaves the contradictions open. The גמרא will not leave פסוקים clashing. Whoever asked them, the problems are real and need solving.

phrases.english: In any case, the verses contradict each other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and goes back to the three contradictions from step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The three pairs of verses from ישעיה and the תורה that מנשה pointed out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ישעיה's words seem to clash with משה רבינו's words, and the clash was never answered in the story

steps.title: Seeing ה׳: a clear glass and an unclear glass
steps.stepSummary: ישעיה's 'I saw ה׳' is explained with a ברייתא. Other נביאים saw through an unclear glass, while משה רבינו saw through a clear one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I saw ה׳' should be understood as the ברייתא teaches: all the נביאים looked through a glass that does not shine clearly, but משה רבינו looked through a glass that shines clearly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the first contradiction: how could ישעיה say he saw ה׳, if the תורה says no person can see ה׳ and live?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים are talking about different kinds of seeing. ישעיה, like all the other נביאים, saw through an unclear glass, so his vision was not a true, direct seeing. Only משה רבינו saw through a clear glass. So ישעיה's words do not clash with the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip it around. The CLEAR glass is the higher level, and it belongs only to משה רבינו. ישעיה's 'seeing' was through the unclear glass.

phrases.english: "I saw Hashem" is as it was taught in a ברייתא:
All the prophets looked
through a looking glass that does not shine clearly,
Moshe our teacher looked
through the looking glass that shines clearly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first of the three contradictions raised in step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing levels of prophecy (the פסוקים talk about different kinds of seeing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ישעיה claimed to see ה׳ directly, which the תורה says is impossible
steps.terutzMaskana: ישעיה saw through an unclear glass, which is not a direct seeing; only משה רבינו saw clearly

steps.title: When ה׳ is near: an individual versus a community
steps.stepSummary: 'Seek ה׳ while He can be found' is about an individual, while the תורה's 'whenever we call Him' is about a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Seek ה׳ while He may be found': this one is about an individual, and that one is about a community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction: ישעיה suggests ה׳ can be found only at certain times, but the תורה says He is near whenever we call.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק is talking about a different group. When a community prays, ה׳ is always near. ישעיה's 'while He may be found' is about one person praying alone, who has special times.

keyTerms.meaning: This one... that one (used to split two cases)

phrases.english: "Seek ה׳ while He may be found":
This one is about an individual, that one is about a community.
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is ישעיה's פסוק (the individual); the second is the תורה's 'whenever we call Him' (the community).

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּרְשׁוּ ה׳ בְּהִמָּצְאוֹ הָא בְּיָחִיד הָא בְּצִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second of the three contradictions
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בכך הא בכך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ישעיה limits ה׳'s nearness to special times, against the תורה's 'always'
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה means a community, which is always answered; ישעיה means an individual, who has special times

steps.title: When is ה׳ near to an individual?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the special time is when an individual can 'find' ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when is that time for an individual?
steps.whatsHappening: The last answer said an individual has a special time when ה׳ 'may be found', so the גמרא asks when that time is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'while He may be found' raises an obvious follow-up: which time is that? The גמרא wants the answer from step 13 to point to a real time.

phrases.english: And for an individual, when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up question on the answer in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific time when ה׳ is near to an individual

steps.title: The ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says an individual's special time is the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: these are the ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the time when ה׳ 'may be found' by an individual is the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the answer to the second contradiction. A community is always answered. An individual has a special window of ten days each year when ה׳ is especially near.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the special strength of the עשרת ימי תשובה, the ten days of return, for each person's prayers.
steps.whatToRemember: Community prayer: ה׳ is always near. Individual prayer: ה׳ is especially near during the ten days from ראש השנה to יום הכיפורים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
These are the ten days
that are between Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אֵלּוּ עֲשָׂרָה יָמִים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten days between ראש השנה and יום הכיפורים

steps.title: Adding years: a disagreement between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: For the third contradiction, about adding years to a life, the גמרא says it depends on a disagreement between תנאים. It starts quoting the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I will fill the number of your days': this is a disagreement between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: 'I will fill the number of your days',
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the third contradiction by saying it depends on an argument between תנאים. It starts quoting the ברייתא, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether a person's years are fixed, as 'I will fill the number of your days' seems to say, or whether years can be added, as ישעיה said. Instead of a simple answer, the גמרא says the תנאים disagree about how to read the פסוק. The details of each opinion come next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a disagreement between תנאים

phrases.english: "I will fill the number of your days":
it is a disagreement between tanna'im, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
"I will fill the number of your days,"

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תורה says a person's years are fixed, against ישעיה's adding of years
